data.title: Clindamycin (topical gel + oral)
data.body:
_Topicals · II Antibacterials_

**Class:** Lincosamide antibiotic (topical)

## Mechanism of action
- Binds the 50S ribosomal subunit → inhibits bacterial protein synthesis (bacteriostatic)
- Reduces C. acnes and the free fatty acids it produces; anti-inflammatory (reduces neutrophil chemotaxis)
- Phosphate ester is inactive until hydrolysed in the skin

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Inflammatory acne vulgaris (papules, pustules) — always combined with benzoyl peroxide (BPO) to prevent resistance
- Folliculitis, hidradenitis suppurativa (mild, Hurley I), rosacea (alternative), pitted keratolysis, erythrasma
- Also in the anti-acne list (group VII)

## Dose & formulations
- Thin layer once or twice daily
- Fixed combinations: clindamycin 1% + BPO 2.5–5%; clindamycin 1.2% + tretinoin 0.025%; clindamycin + adapalene; clindamycin + nicotinamide
- Do not use as monotherapy and limit to about 12 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Dryness, peeling, irritation
- C. acnes and staphylococcal resistance with monotherapy
- C. difficile colitis is very rare (case reports)

## Contraindications
- History of inflammatory bowel disease or antibiotic-associated colitis
- Hypersensitivity to lincomycin/clindamycin

## Drug interactions
- Erythromycin topical — antagonism (both act at 50S)

## Pregnancy & lactation
Safe in pregnancy (preferred topical antibiotic with BPO).

## Viva points
- Never use topical antibiotics alone for acne — always with BPO (resistance)
- Safe in pregnancy
- Rare pseudomembranous colitis — ask about bowel disease

## Oral form: Clindamycin oral
_Lincosamide (oral/IV)_

**Mechanism**
- 50S ribosomal inhibitor; also suppresses toxin production by staphylococci and streptococci (useful in necrotising infections)

**Indications**
- Hidradenitis suppurativa: clindamycin 300 mg + rifampicin 300 mg twice daily for 10–12 weeks
- Staphylococcal/streptococcal skin infections in penicillin allergy; community MRSA (if sensitive)
- Necrotising fasciitis and toxic shock syndrome (with penicillin — antitoxin effect); anaerobic infections; BV (oral/vaginal)

**Dose & how to apply**
- 150–450 mg four times daily (adults); children 10–25 mg/kg/day

**Adverse effects**
- Diarrhoea and C. difficile pseudomembranous colitis (classic association)
- Rash, metallic taste, hepatitis (rare)

**Contraindications**
- History of antibiotic-associated colitis

**Interactions**
- Neuromuscular blockers (potentiated); erythromycin (antagonism)

**Pregnancy:** Acceptable in pregnancy.

**Viva points**
- Clindamycin + rifampicin for hidradenitis
- Antitoxin effect in toxic shock
- Classic cause of C. difficile colitis

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.41 (Topical antibacterials); Khopkar ch.18; Khopkar ch.1; Wolverton 4e ch.9 and ch.41. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
